claims.text: Increasing configurational entropy through enhanced atomic mixing creates local lattice strain variations.
Increasing configurational entropy through enhanced atomic mixing creates electronic inhomogeneity.
Local lattice strain and electronic inhomogeneity facilitate electron pairing.
Increasing configurational entropy promotes the onset and robustness of low-temperature superconductivity.
The starting sample has relatively low configurational entropy because it has a minimal level of atomic mixing.
The starting alloy's superconducting performance is uncharacterized or weak.
Alloy variants should be fabricated with greater constituent-element diversity and mixing ratios to increase configurational entropy.
Superconductivity is expected to be especially sensitive to local structural and electronic fluctuations below 5 K.
Enhanced configurational entropy broadens the distribution of local bonding environments.
Local lattice strain and electronic-density fluctuations lower the effective electron-pairing energy barrier.
Lowering the effective pairing barrier produces stronger or more coherent pairing and a superconducting state at low temperature.
Higher-configurational-entropy samples will have greater critical current density than the lower-entropy baseline.
Higher-configurational-entropy samples may have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the lower-entropy baseline.
The proposed entropy effect is limited primarily to temperatures below approximately 5 K.
At higher temperatures, mechanisms such as phonon scattering may dominate and prevent the proposed effect from persisting.
Beyond an optimal configurational-entropy range, excessive disorder may reduce electron mobility and suppress superconducting performance.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing higher- and lower-entropy samples under identical low-temperature measurement conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in both Tc and Jc would falsify the proposed beneficial effect of increased configurational entropy.
Failure of measured structural or electronic variations to correlate with superconducting performance would falsify the proposed mechanism.
